whyMainnetExists: MiniKit refuses to send a transaction on any chain but World Chain mainnet. From @worldcoin/minikit-js 2.0.3's own send-transaction source: `var WORLD_CHAIN_ID = 480; ... if (chainId !== WORLD_CHAIN_ID) throw new SendTransactionError('invalid_operation', { reason: 'World App only supports World Chain (chainId: 480)' })`. The check is client-side and unconditional, and MiniKit's EIP-1193 provider also hardcodes eth_chainId to 0x1e0. So a Mini App user on World Chain Sepolia (4801) could sign in but could never transact — enroll, vouch and claim all failed with 'invalid_operation'. No flag or config changes this; the only fix is contracts on 480.

addressBook.what: World ID's REAL Address Book — 3095 bytes of code, confirmed live on chain 480 before deploying against it.
addressBook.differenceFromSepolia: The Sepolia deployment could not use this: the Address Book exists on World Chain mainnet ONLY, which is why contracts/script/GenesisAnchorBook.sol was written as a testnet stand-in. Here it is the real contract, so AvalRegistry.isAnchor() is answered by genuine Orb verification and anchorSource() returns 'world-id-orb', not 'genesis-testnet'.

verifiedOnChain.method: eth_getCode on every address, plus getters read back with cast — not taken from the deploy script's own output.

wiring.readAt: re-read with cast against the LIVE redeployed registry after E-18, not carried over from the superseded deployment

isAnchorAfterE18Fix.note: Read with cast against the redeployed AvalRegistry. Proves the corrected addressVerifiedUntil interface resolves real Orb status instead of reverting.

verifiedOnChain.correction: deployedAtBlock and AvalRegistry codeBytes were both wrong in the first version of this file: 32833180 and 7637. 7637 is the SUPERSEDED pre-E-18 registry's size, carried over by mistake; the live one is 7645 because the isAnchor fix changed the bytecode. The deploy receipt puts the constructor in block 32833177. Both re-read from chain (eth_getCode, cast receipt), not edited by hand.

noSeededGraph: Deliberate. On Sepolia the anchor set was seeded through GenesisAnchorBook, which let alice/bob/anchor1-6/ring1-6 exist and made the 6-account collusion ring provable on chain. Here the anchor set is World ID's real Orb registry, so those generated keys are not anchors and the trust-math demonstration is NOT reproducible on this chain — it lives on worldchain-sepolia.json. The consequence to state plainly: every Orb-verified human who enrolls here is a depth-0 anchor with a FIXED score of 100 that ignores all inbound vouches (errata E-6), so on this deployment vouching for a verified human changes nothing. That is the spec behaving as written (docs/03-worldid.md §3.1), and it contradicts the product's own thesis that proof-of-human is the floor rather than the ladder.
notes: ENS is unaffected and remains on Ethereum Sepolia (deployments/ens-sepolia.json, ens-members-sepolia.json) — a different chain entirely, already working, all 17 member names and their per-member registries live there.
The World ID app ID and RP ID are unchanged and work against mainnet as-is.

governor == deployer here, so the eight post-deploy wiring setters ran in the same script. A real deployment would make governor a 2-of-3 multisig and submit those separately (docs/02-contracts.md §6).

The attestor is deliberately NOT the deployer: attestations are signed by 0x69827C0F..., the key the app already holds as ATTESTOR_PRIVATE_KEY, while the deployer key only ever deployed. Losing one does not immediately grant the other's power.

supersededFirstDeployment.reason: Redeployed after errata E-18: IAddressBook declared getIsUserVerified(address)->bool, which does not exist on World ID's real Address Book, so isAnchor() reverted for every address on mainnet. These contracts are DEAD — do not use.
